about: Content shape → scene component. Each entry is a STARTING POINT, never a fence: combine, bend or ignore any of them, or invent a new form from the runtime primitives. No gate reads this file; gates judge outcomes only (S1–S8, C1–C8, density, determinism).
how_to_choose: Name the content SHAPE first (what the narration is doing: weighing, counting, travelling, failing…), then pick the component.
Read not_this: if a neighbour fits better, use the neighbour.
A 3-column table that says the same thing wins over a fancier scene.
Over budget → split into an overview scene plus a detail scene, or pass overBudget:'<reason>' explicitly.

invented_form.how: Draw with the runtime primitives (card, text, chip, node, connector, asset, cursor, mark) and call z.declareForm({invented:'<name>', reason:'<why no catalog entry fits>'}).

fields.invented: a short name for the new form
fields.reason: one sentence: why it teaches this better

invented_form.rule: An invented form passes or fails on the same outcome gates as a catalog component — never on catalog membership.

contract.call: S.<component>(scene, props) — draws inside a section named props.section or the component id
contract.timing: every 'at'/'enter' is a named beat ('the-router') or a spoken word {line, word, occurrence}; numbers are rejected
contract.kit: colours, type sizes, radius and motion come from the active kit (window.__C8_KIT__)
contract.determinism: no clock, no Math.random; layout jitter (network) uses the seeded C8.random(seed), recorded in the trace

common_props.enter: beat or word that brings the component in (required)
common_props.title: optional heading
common_props.ghost: false hides the slot outlines of items not yet reached
common_props.overBudget: a reason string that opts out of the item budget

types.use_when: Two independent axes (e.g. speed × freshness) and the four combinations they produce; the point is which quadrant a choice lands in.

not_this.when: more than two attributes per option

types.example: caching: fresh vs fast, the TTL cache quadrant highlighted

types.use_when: Exactly two options judged on one scale, where the narration says which one outweighs the other.

not_this.when: the options differ on several attributes
a quantity per option against a target

types.example: feature flag vs full deploy, tilting to the flag

types.use_when: A total that grows (or shrinks) as each spoken line adds one entry; the viewer should watch the sum change.

not_this.when: one final number matters, not the steps
the entries are stages that lose volume

types.example: retry cost counted retry by retry

types.use_when: One request, packet or item moving from a start to a destination, possibly via waypoints; the travel itself is the idea.

not_this.when: several steps each transform the item

types.example: browser → gateway → billing, the token arriving on 'billing'

types.use_when: The same system in two states, where the change between them is the point (what the fix, cache or migration changed).

not_this.when: more than two states in a cycle

types.example: page latency before and after a shared cache

types.use_when: One subject passing through a repeating or closed sequence of states; the current state moves as the narration does.

not_this.when: the states never loop and each does work

types.example: an order: created → paid → shipped → delivered

types.use_when: Volume shrinking stage by stage; the lost share between stages is the message.

not_this.when: stages do work but volume is constant

types.example: sign-up page → form → verified email

types.use_when: Something broke: quote the one line that carries the meaning, say why, say what to change.

not_this.when: a chain of causes leads to the failure

types.example: SchemaError on an unexpected column, with cause and fix

types.use_when: Events where WHEN they happened matters (an incident, a release history); dates or times label each event.

not_this.when: order matters but time does not

types.example: an incident from deploy to recovery

types.use_when: Layers that a request crosses or that build on each other (network stack, middleware, storage tiers).

not_this.when: the layers are peers, not stacked
each layer transforms the item in order

types.example: edge → auth → service → storage, auth in focus

types.use_when: Several sources converging on one consumer (aggregation, a bottleneck, a merge).

not_this.when: the many are stages in order

types.example: three regional feeds into one aggregator

types.use_when: One producer broadcasting to several consumers (publish/subscribe, a dispatcher).
types.example: one order event read by billing, shipping and email

types.use_when: A staged process where each stage does work on the item and hands it on; the stage being explained is highlighted.

not_this.when: one item travelling, stages do nothing

types.example: ingest → clean → score → publish

types.use_when: Options compared on three or more attributes; a 3-column table that says the same thing as a diagram wins.
types.example: three queue options on ordering, cost and replay

types.use_when: A single quantity is the payoff; it counts up and lands on the spoken word that names it.

not_this.when: the number is the sum of steps worth showing

types.example: 12,000 requests per second, landing on 'thousand'

types.use_when: The proof is a quoted line, a document passage or a screenshot; show it verbatim with its source.

not_this.when: the proof is a line of code to point at
the proof is a region of a bigger screen

types.example: the timeout line and the dashboard that shows it

types.use_when: One line of code decides the behaviour; show the surrounding lines, light up the deciding one, cite path:line.

not_this.when: a quote from prose or a log

types.example: router.py:88 sending an order to review

types.use_when: Regions, boundaries or trust zones; what sits where and what crosses a boundary.
types.example: public web, gateway and a private network boundary

types.use_when: A decision with forks, or a whole broken into parts; every fork has labelled exits.

not_this.when: the branches never rejoin and there is only one path

types.example: a refund decided by age and amount

types.use_when: Parties exchanging messages over time (request/response, a handshake); time runs down the page.
types.example: app → API → user store → token

types.use_when: One measure against a limit; which side of the threshold it sits on is the message.

not_this.when: no limit, the number alone matters

types.example: disk use at 86% against an 80% alarm

types.use_when: A value per (row, column) where the pattern — the hot spot — is the point; ink is one hue at stepped opacity.
types.example: errors by region and hour, west at noon highlighted

types.use_when: Criteria that are met or unmet; status is shown by shape AND word, never by hue alone.
types.example: a release checklist with the load test failing

types.use_when: Many-to-many relationships (who calls whom); seeded deterministic layout, and no edge is drawn behind an unrelated node.
types.example: five services with orders as the hub

types.use_when: One region of something larger is what matters; keep the whole visible and show the region enlarged beside it.

not_this.when: the whole is not needed for context
the detail is a code line

types.example: the failed-payments panel of an operations dashboard

types.use_when: A causal chain where each step makes the next happen; the first cause and the final effect are marked.

not_this.when: the steps are deliberate stages of a process

types.example: a pool-size typo that took checkout down

types.use_when: A few quantities compared with each other and with a budget or baseline; bar length carries the value.
types.example: build time per target against a ten-minute budget
